newsitem.title: NORWAY: DnB books healthy H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: DnB books healthy H1 profits.

text.p: Den norske Bank (DnB), Norway's largest bank, on Wednesday recorded net profits of 1,494 million crowns ($193 million) in the first half of 1997, compared with 1,489 million in the corresponding period last year.
Return on equity was 20.8 percent compared with 23.3 percent while earnings per share were 2.33 crowns after 2.32 crowns, the bank said in a statement.

Second-quarter profits totalled 674 million crowns, as against 820 million in the first quarter. Pre-tax operating profits before loan losses were 1,343 million in the first half, up 72 million on the corresponding period last year.

"DnB has shown healthy profits and sound progress so far this year," group managing director Finn Hvistendahl said. "The group is currently experiencing strong growth in all areas of business and brisk activity in the development of new service concepts."
The group's range of products and market coverage are being expanded, such as through the acquisition of mortgage lender BNbank this year, the bank said.
In spite of a rise in lending of close to 10 percent, the total computed credit risk remains unchanged, it said.

"The accounts show that the narrowing of interest margins is abating, while income other than interest income shows a continued rise," Hvistendahl said. "We are just starting to see a rise in sales and income as a result of extensive cooperation between the various units within the group."

He said one example was the increasing profit contribution from insurance subsidiary Vital. During the first half, 86 million crowns were taken to income as owner's share of profits in Vital, up 23 million on the corresponding period last year.

Following several years characterised by a continuous squeeze on the bank's interest margins, the second-quarter accounts show a total margin of 2.69 per cent for customer deposits and lending, on a level with the margin for the first quarter, DnB said.
Net interest income totalled 2.14 billion in the first half of 1997, up from 2.12 million.
Average lending rose by 11.7 per cent from the first half of 1996, providing a 148 million crown boost to interest income.

Other operating income came to 1.53 billion in the first half, up 113 million. Commissions and fees receivable on banking services showed a strong rise, stemming mainly from income on custodial services. Income on payment services and securities trading also showed a positive trend.
Net gains on foreign exchange and financial instruments totalled 477 million crowns, up from 454 million.
Operating expenses totalled 2.33 billion crowns for the first six months, up 70 million or 3.1 per cent.
"The increase reflects a higher level of activity, expanding business volumes and extensive development projects," DnB said.

The DnB Group recorded 161 million crowns in net reversals on previous loan losses for the year to date, as compared with 226 million in the first half of 1996. The level of new losses was reduced from 503 million in the first half of 1996 to 366 million in the first half of this year.

The volume of non-performing and doubtful commitments has been further reduced. At end-June, problem commitments totalled 4.21 billion after deductions of specified loan-loss provisions, compared with 4.62 billion at the beginning of the year, the bank said.
The group charged 11 million in taxes to the accounts for the first half. This primarily represents taxes for the bank's foreign branches.

No tax charges have been calculated on the parent bank's Norwegian operations for 1997. The calculation of the tax charge is based on acceptance of the bank's view in two current disputes with Norwegian tax authorities.
The group's total assets rose from 189.8 billion crowns as at December 31, 1996 to 218.4 billion as at June 30 this year. ($ = 7.739 Norwegian Crowns)
